originality.rationale: An exact 21-orbit and (5,1,1,1,1) scheme refinement for two geometrically smooth cubic members over F2 is not implied by the inspected primary theorems. Kaplan--Matei assumes q>2 for its general pair-count theorem and does not require both smooth; Asgarli--Ghioca requires all rational pencil members smooth whereas the present third member is reducible. Exact equivalent assertions were not found in targeted literature and relevant research-record searches. An unindexed earlier F2 cubic-table incidence analysis is a residual risk, not proven absent.
residual_risks: Older unindexed classifications of binary elliptic cubic equations or finite-plane pair-incidence catalogues may contain equivalent orbit data or contact multiplicities.

Some historically relevant primary texts concerning individual nonsingular plane cubics were only accessible by index/abstract, not fully examined; individual point counts alone do not imply the present pair theorem.

value.rationale: A complete classification of maximal intersections of geometrically smooth genus-one plane cubics over the smallest finite field, together with a forced exceptional length-five scheme contact and three-line reducible pencil member. These refine rational-point incidence data into geometric structure and provide a motivated sharp extremal answer rather than an arbitrary count.
